text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Kosovo is an internal affair of Yugoslavia which is committed to settling the issue through dialogue with the Albanian national minority, says Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic in a lengthy interview to Moscow daily Pravda.
- Exhibition of Greek products to be held at Belgrade fair from November 21 to 25.
- European computer producer Siemens Nicksdorf officially returns to Yugoslav market signing a deal on sales and servicing of its products with Belgrade firm IBIS-SYS.
- Belgrade Beobanka and representatives of the South Afican Farmers' Union sign a cooperation protocol in Belgrade Tuesday.
- Yugoslavia will organise a large economic exhibition in Greece from December 3 to 7.
- Serbia hopes to earn $700 million from agriculture exports in 1997, the Serbian chamber of economy said.
- International exhibition of household equipment grouping producers from Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Austria and Britain to be held at Belgrade fair from December 3 to 7.
- The Belgrade electoral commission announces preliminary results of local elections in which opposition Zajedno won the majority of 60 seats in the 110 seat municipal assembly.
- Interpol sends data on stolen cars to Yugoslav police authorities estimating there are between 25 and 30 thousand such cars in Yugoslavia, the Bosnian Serb Republic and eastern Slavonia.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian opposition leaders say they will not allow their victory at local elections to be turned into defeat and warn about forged election results.

- The visiting World Bank delegation is in Yugoslavia to present its report on development and to get to know the situation but time is not yet ripe for talks with the government on Yugoslavia's relations with the Bank, says Ilham Zuryk, a member of the bank delegation.
- Bosnian Serb Prime Minister Gojko Klickovic says former Bosnian Serb army commander general Ratko Mladic will formally hand over his duties to the new commander general Pero Colic on Wednesday.
- Nasa Borba unofficially learns that present director of Radio Television Serbia Dragoljub Milanovic was sacked by Milosevic over badly conducted election propaganda.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- The first sessions of the newly elected municipal and city assemblies to be held at the latest 20 days after elections which is December 7 for most municipalities.
BORBA
- Representatives of multinational company ABB and president of Yugoslav chamber of economy Mihajlo Milojevic speak about possible joint construction of thermo electric power plant in Kosovo.
- Coal reserves in Kosovo stand at 15.5 billion tonnes according to a study of the Belgrade Mining and Geology faculty.
- Over 100 Czech firms to organise presentation of their programmes in Belgrade from December 3 to 7.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Serbian finance ministry and other republican ministries to prepare documentation needed for deciding about Yugoslavia's reintegration in international financial organisations, it was agreed during meeting of the World Bank delegation and Serbian finance minister Dusan Vlatkovic.
-- Belgrade Newsroom, 381 11 222 4254
